source.note: R185. The first 157 characters are the put-to-move phrasing R182 measured as the winning sentence's live half and are untouched, so the round is a statement about the tail. The 197 characters it replaces were the format instruction, and R183 showed that instruction is inert on the `any-line` channel: the reader executes a command on a later line, so telling the model to write one does not change what the world receives. What the nine lost `put` games show instead is a take from a closed container answering `Nothing happens.`, with every put after it failing the same way -- 12.33 invalid actions per lost game against 1.60 in a won one. 551 rendered characters, one entry.
operations_written: open the container before taking from it
operations_replaced: one command per turn, on its own line
source.provenance: written after R184 closed the budget as an explanation and split the nine lost `put` games into five that issue commands the world rejects and four that run out of turns mid-progress

entries.text: If a "put" action repeatedly fails despite being at the correct location and holding the object, try the alternative phrasing "move <object> to <receptacle>". A closed container hides its contents: open the cabinet, fridge, drawer or safe before taking anything from it, or the take answers "Nothing happens." and the put that follows fails the same way.
